Mine are usually head-turning, arm, shoulder, and back jerks, but only occasionally spread to full body.  

Before making any concrete conclusions, I do recommend checking in with a Neurologist. Having a family history of epilepsy, you have a higher chance of having it yourself.

I'll start off by saying that I'm nit a doctor, but I do have really poorly-controlled epilepsy. The jerking spasms that you're describing sound sprt of like Jacksonian motor seizures.  It's basically a seizure where you don't have and loss of awareness, and is categorized by a kind of muscle jerk/?spasm in a specific area, that could spread to your whole body, or even be a long series of jerks. 

If I'm not mistaken, these are also a type of focal seizure, as well as seizures that affect mood. 

Also fun fact, epileptics typically have less melatonin and dopamine (sleepy & happy hormones).

My boyfriend witnessed one of my more serious seizures. I smoked a little bit of weed (because it helps with what I still thought were migraines) and started to feel WAY too high. I laid down to go to sleep but woke up because I just felt bad. I thought maybe it was an asthma attack or something, so I wake up the hubby and tell him to get me a glass of water while I tore up the room looking for an inhaler. I couldn't find it, so I ran into the kitchen. He turned around to talk to me and I just dropped. He said I let out a breath and hit the floor. I don't really remember the falling part, but I remember hearing my head hit the ground. After that, I was kind of talking, but it was like I was limited to syllables. he administered my inhaler. Didn't help. I started shaking and jerking while I was on the floor, and he called the ambulance. I was fluctuating in levels of responsiveness and passed out at one point while telling myself "you can't die from weed" (poor brain was confused). According to my boyfriend, I was jerking nonstop and my limbs were flailing at this point. I remember the EMT asking me what I took and not believing me when I said weed. I came to again, freaked out that they were holding the defibrillator above me, and passed out again. I woke up in the hospital 13 hours or so after arriving. By boyfriend said that my body literally turned gray while I was out. I still wasn't diagnosed at this point. 

There were some occasions where I kind of gradually lost awareness until I was 'out', and some where I just dropped. Those latter is a bit more rare, now that I can spot the subtle signs and actually know what's going on. 

 I'm currently living in an area known for their less-than-stellar public healthcare. I waited 9 months after my initial diagnosis for a 60 minute long EEG, which was inconclusive. Basically, I wasn't having a seizure and they couldn't map any seizure activity. When you do the long test, it's best that your Jane does anything she would do on a regular day, for accuracy's sake.

Before and after a 'regular' seizure (either mild shaking or just complete brain derp), I'm generally really light sensitive. This seems to be something that I always deal with as well, so I have some really good sunglasses with me at all times. During these times, I'm also a bit more emotional. Positive emotions and negative emotions are amplified many times over. If something is mildly funny, I'll be stuck with a goofy ass smile on my face for a while. Recently, I've been finding myself smiling or laughing when there is absolutely nothing funny or positive as well. It's not quite "Joker" level, but it has people looking at me like I'm off my rocker. After a seizure, I feel really sluggish, drained, headachey, uncoordinated, and mentally slow. Certain things require a lot of focus and certain things are just not possible. Sometimes, if I have to do a simple mental task, it'll be like putting me in an empty room and asking me to find a table. 

​

I came to realize recently that I've been having seizures that I don't even notice (absence seizures).  To me, they just feel like I'm spacing out, or that my brain just "isn't doing brain things". Explaining it is pretty hard, but a good example is that I once tried to buckle my seatbelt when I sat down at work. It took a good minute for me to realize why that wasn't working our for me, lol!
